_doc: Single source of truth for the generated-file banner injected by all workflow engines. Edit this file to change the stamp shape/wording — every engine that sources inject-header.sh picks up the new template on next build. Placeholders interpolated at build time: {{SOURCE}}, {{ENGINE}}, {{REBUILD_CMD}}.
template: ║   Manual edits will be overwritten on next build.                ║
_json_policy_doc: JSON cannot carry comments, so generated JSON is stamped two ways instead: a `_generated` meta-object hoisted to the top of the root object, AND a human-readable notice folded into `description` (the field a person or an LLM actually reads first). Stamping is ON BY DEFAULT — a generated file that does not say it is generated gets hand-edited and silently reverted on the next build, which is the exact failure this engine exists to prevent. Opt out per-file via `json_skip_basenames` (schema-strict formats, or files whose `description` is semantically consumed downstream), or per-run via INJECT_JSON=0.
json_notice_template: ⚠ GENERATED — DO NOT EDIT · SoT: {{SOURCE}} · Engine: {{ENGINE}} · Rebuild: {{REBUILD_CMD}}

enforced_scopes._doc: Scope roots for 9_others/test/test_service_header_present.sh. Each entry is a directory glob, relative to the repo root, whose immediate subdirectories are services carrying build.json. The tester asserts every scope is REACHABLE: a glob that matches no directory, or a scope that contributes zero in-scope files, is a FAILURE and never a quiet pass. Before 2026-09-16 the three scopes were hardcoded as three copy-pasted blocks in the tester, and a_solutions/ was reached by a glob that iterates zero times when it is absent — so the container engine, the scope the tester exists for, could vanish entirely while the run still printed 'PASS (304 files checked)' from the other two. Add a scope HERE, not in the script.
